SK Group immediately invested $3.5B in the first year, despite the chip market remaining depressed. [...] Only five years ago, SK Hynix's NAND segment was widely viewed as a loss-making “secondary” business. The acquisition of Solidigm (a semiconductor subsidiary) for $9B from Intel in 2021 has helped turn around this segment. The company has strategically moved away from the volatile consumer SSD market to prioritize high-margin enterprise SSDs (eSSDs) for AI data centers. This pivot towards specialized, high-capacity storage has further boosted the company’s profitability and overall margins.
